SNS・note（note・本文）.quote: "Monolith-type AI": Examination of high-speed recognition and ease of implementation in a 3D lattice-type predictive coding reservoir｜青い鴉（ぶるくろ）
"Monolith-type AI": Examination of high-speed recognition and ease of implementation in a 3D lattice-type predictive coding reservoir

In this study, we propose "Monolith," a 3D lattice-type neural circuit model that fuses Predictive Coding (PC), based on the brain's Active Inference, with the concept of Reservoir Computing (RC). This model consists of a 3D lattice of 512 units with fixed internal connection weights, and extracts the "prediction error loss," which is the discrepancy between input signals and internal predictions,

Conventional deep learning (Backpropagation) faces challenges with high computational costs and wiring complexity associated with global error propagation. In contrast, the brain processes information efficiently through the minimization of local prediction errors. Therefore, there is an argument that intelligence can be implemented at a lower cost.
This study explores a new form of intelligence,
, which achieves both biological plausibility and engineering ease of implementation by running PC (Predictive Coding) within a reservoir that has a physical 3D spatial structure.
: A grid structure of 8 x 8 x 8 = 512 units in total. Each unit is connected to 26 neighboring cells with random fixed weights W.
